content.title: About
content.content: Grits are coarsely ground corn kernels, traditionally cooked in water or milk. The cheese version adds grated cheese, giving the dish a creamy flavor and boosting its protein content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grits are a staple breakfast in the Southern United States.
Corn, the base of grits, is one of the oldest cultivated crops in the Americas.
Cheese can be cheddar, mozzarella, or any meltable variety.
Grits can be adapted to dietary needs by using plant‑based milks.
Traditionally grits are cooked to a creamy consistency, but they can also be prepared more loosely.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Grits provide slowly digestible energy, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Cheese adds a substantial amount of complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Cheese is a good source of calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Corn supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low fat when using reduced‑fat cheese
items.content: Choosing low‑fat cheese varieties can keep the dish lower in calories.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Many cheeses are salty; people monitoring sodium intake should opt for low‑salt options.

items.title: Gluten in processed mixes
items.content: Some pre‑made grits mixes contain gluten additives; check labels if you follow a gluten‑free diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, often topped with butter, herbs, or crisp bacon. Grits with cheese can be a side dish for meats or a hearty breakfast on their own.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry grits in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked grits should be cooled and stored in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days.
